engines.name: eduengine — modular education supply/demand/shadow-education ABM
engines.path: engine/eduengine/ (core.py, measure.py, ledger.py, planning.py, struts.py, settle.py, modules/{state,schools,labour,tutoring,sdg4,anchor}.py); built by engine/worlds.py
engines.version: v0.1–v0.4 features in source comments (CORE_DEFAULTS v0.3 additions; tutoring/state modules v0.x)
engines.type: synthetic agent/cohort simulation (not national regression model)
engines.status: toy/uncalibrated: engine/worlds.py docstring 'Toy worlds: abstractions, not countries ... nothing is calibrated'; used by the audited staging experiment (worlds.formal_loop)
state_variables: children: cohort (entry year), grade g (0-15, 16 grades), learning L (grade-equivalents), credential, attendance status, started/reason, ability a, home capital, household income y, urban flag, parity
households: income, consumption need, liquidity/borrowing, shocks, child-wage schedule
schools/supply: public budget, teachers, class size, quality q_pub, private entry, tuition/fees
labour: formal vacancies per entrant, credential floors, queues, informal wages, wage bill
fiscal: tax revenue (formal + consumption), education share of tax revenue, CCT
tutoring: own-teacher vs firm supply, buy-back/gate-prep/remedial motives, prices
stage_transitions: annual continuation vs stop vs repeat (promotion bar; household liquidity)
primary (6 grades) -> lower secondary gate -> lower (3) -> upper-secondary gate -> upper (3) -> tertiary gate -> tertiary (4)
gates: absolute bar thresholds or planned quota seats (share x cohort), fail->track or stop
leavers enter labour market: formal queue by credential vs informal/competitive
engines.supply_vs_demand: separate modules: PublicSchools/PrivateSchools (supply, financing), demand through household utility (discount future income, child wage, costs, beliefs)
engines.rural_migration: NOT SIMULATED: rural is a household attribute (urban flag) plus an extra schooling cost (rural_cost=0.03 beyond primary) and lower tutoring firm access; no rural-urban migration, no remittances, no location transitions, no spatial labour market
engines.jobs_formalization_credential: QueueLabour: formal vacancies per entrant (vac0), credential floors, graduate queue, informality (Harris-Todaro), wage premium beliefs; optional job_elasticity feedback (vacancies x educated share^elasticity) is an ASSUMED functional form
engines.quality_shadow_tutoring: quality from class size/teacher pay/monitoring/withholding; tutoring market with own-teacher buy-back, gate-prep and remedial motives, rural firm access and bans
engines.heterogeneity: household income (lognormal), urban/rural, ability, home capital; cohort-by-year variation

engines.name: MASSENG v5 — portable national cohort-flow model of massification (PHL v1–v5; KHM v3; HKG facts)
engines.version: v5 (PROTOCOL_v5, written 2026-11-22 before first fit); archived v1-v4 protocols preserved; R0-R5 specifications
engines.type: deterministic cohort-flow/regression hybrid fitted to country data (PHL/KHM); 'the actual PHL MASSENG v5 R1 model' used by the Bayesian screens
engines.status: fitted for PHL (v5 fits R0-R5, fit_R1.json = R1 spec with b_h,b_p,b_r,lam fitted) and KHM (v3 fits); retrospective and inspected (post-1995 seen per PROTOCOL_v5)
state_variables: status: entrants, enrolled, repeaters, deferred/qualified-waiting (tertiary deferral pool), completers, out-of-school
demand utility: human-capital premium (b_h), positional credential share (b_p), relational/formal-work floor (b_r), declining cost sensitivity (lam), level intercepts, income decile
supply/financing: public capacity, vouchers, fees/subsidies, free tuition, CCT, cycle rules
stage_transitions: Grade 1 entry -> primary (6) -> secondary (3) [gate at end of secondary] -> upper-secondary (3) [senior-high reform gates] -> tertiary (4)
repetition (rep_prim/rep_sec), late entry (late), dropout, upper-secondary transition (PHL Grade 10->11)
tertiary deferral pool (qualified waiting) and admission when capacity/utility allows
engines.supply_vs_demand: supply/financing facts enter as inputs (capacity, vouchers, fees, subsidies); demand engine is the fitted part
engines.rural_migration: NOT MODELLED: model is national by income decile; no region/rural dimension, no migration
engines.jobs_formalization_credential: relational floor b_r on formal-work share (wage/salary employment proxy); wage premiums for next credential are drivers; credential queues are NOT an explicit employer queue in v5 (unlike eduengine)
engines.quality_shadow_tutoring: NOT MODELLED in v5: no school quality, learning, or tutoring; v6 Phase-1 prototype adds stage/work states but not quality/tutoring yet
engines.heterogeneity: income deciles, cohorts, public/private, gender not modelled
limitations: employer credential demand proxied by formal-share driver

engines.name: MASSENG v6 Phase 1 — conserved cohorts and joint admissions (accounting prototype)
engines.version: v6 Phase 1 prototype (README: 'illustrative mechanics; not calibrated, causally identified, or empirically validated')
engines.type: probability-mass cohort accounting kernel with joint admission markets
engines.status: prototype; does NOT yet implement the full country-year v6 simulation; no fitted parameters; synthetic known-answer tests only
state_variables: CohortKey(country, birth_cohort, decile, region, stage, grade, sector, education_status, work_status)
EducationStatus: attending / repeating / qualified_waiting / out_of_school_reenterable / completed / exit_terminal / alternative
stocks by level/sector; entry funnel Q>=L>=E>=R; market capacity/reservations
stage_transitions: conserved cohort progression with explicit external entries/deaths/exits/reentries
joint admissions: effective applicants -> at most one market; continuing reservations respected
engines.supply_vs_demand: EntryFunnel separates latent (Q) -> qualified (L) -> eligible (E) -> effective (R) demand; Market supplies capacity
engines.rural_migration: region is a CohortKey dimension but no migration flows are implemented
engines.jobs_formalization_credential: work_status is recorded orthogonally; no employer queue/credential model yet

engines.name: MASSENG v5 PHL R1 conditional Bayesian-style importance screen
engines.version: prototype importance screen (no resampling; conditional weights)
engines.type: prior-draw importance screening against 1971-1995 PHL GERs
engines.status: committed 256-draw pilots: ESS 5.94 (main) / 1.77 (expanded), holdout GER RMSE 9.645/7.065 vs persistence 6.600; 4096-draw main+expanded runs active on region-42 at audit time (see verification)
state_variables: MASSENG v5 R1 parameters b_h,b_p,b_r,lam drawn; all other params fixed at fit_R1.json
stage_transitions: model simulation per draw; Gaussian pseudo-likelihood; weights; ESS; holdout comparison
limitations: conditional importance weights, not calibrated posterior
fixed nuisance from broader fit = data reuse
